end.summary:
Asha practised identifying standing, sleeping and slanting straight lines.
Om gave 2 unaided correct responses out of 4 attempts.
They described standing lines as vertical and slanting lines as tilted.
They called a cornered or zigzag line curved once; this was not corrected later in the lesson.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised the three types of straight lines using familiar examples such as a goalpost, a flagpole and a slide. Om explained that standing and slanting lines are both straight, but differ in direction, and later correctly said that a slanting line is straight rather than curved. Om mixed up a cornered or zigzag line with a curved line, and this was not corrected later. At home, ask Om to sort drawn examples into standing, sleeping, slanting and curved groups, checking whether each line bends.
